# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
from dataclasses import dataclass

import torch

from vllm.config import CacheConfig
from vllm.model_executor.custom_op import PluggableLayer
from vllm.model_executor.layers.attention import MLAAttention
from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization import QuantizationConfig


@dataclass
class MLAModules:
    """Modules used in MLA."""

    kv_a_layernorm: torch.nn.Module
    kv_b_proj: torch.nn.Module
    rotary_emb: torch.nn.Module
    o_proj: torch.nn.Module
    fused_qkv_a_proj: torch.nn.Module | None
    kv_a_proj_with_mqa: torch.nn.Module | None
    q_a_layernorm: torch.nn.Module | None
    q_b_proj: torch.nn.Module | None
    q_proj: torch.nn.Module | None
    indexer: torch.nn.Module | None
    is_sparse: bool
    topk_indices_buffer: torch.Tensor | None
    indexer_rotary_emb: torch.nn.Module | None = None


# --8<-- [start:multi_head_latent_attention]
@PluggableLayer.register("multi_head_latent_attention")
class MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper(PluggableLayer):
    """Pluggable MLA layer which allows OOT backends to add
    custom implementations of the outer MLA layer (including rope & o_proj).
    Note that currently oot platforms can still use CustomOp.register_oot to
    replace MLA layer entirely, although we use PluggableLayer to register
    this layer now.

    This class takes positions and hidden_states as input.
    The input tensors can either contain prefill tokens or decode tokens.
    The class does the following:

    1. MLA Preprocess.
    2. Perform multi-head attention to prefill tokens and
       multi-query attention to decode tokens separately.
    3. Return the output tensor.
    """

    # --8<-- [end:multi_head_latent_attention]

    def __init__(
        self,
        hidden_size: int,
        num_heads: int,
        scale: float,
        qk_nope_head_dim: int,
        qk_rope_head_dim: int,
        v_head_dim: int,
        q_lora_rank: int | None,
        kv_lora_rank: int,
        mla_modules: MLAModules,
        cache_config: CacheConfig | None = None,
        quant_config: QuantizationConfig | None = None,
        prefix: str = "",
        skip_topk: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.hidden_size = hidden_size
        self.qk_nope_head_dim = qk_nope_head_dim
        self.qk_rope_head_dim = qk_rope_head_dim
        self.qk_head_dim = qk_nope_head_dim + qk_rope_head_dim
        self.v_head_dim = v_head_dim
        self.q_lora_rank = q_lora_rank
        self.kv_lora_rank = kv_lora_rank
        self.num_heads = num_heads
        self.fused_qkv_a_proj = mla_modules.fused_qkv_a_proj
        self.kv_a_proj_with_mqa = mla_modules.kv_a_proj_with_mqa
        self.q_a_layernorm = mla_modules.q_a_layernorm
        self.q_b_proj = mla_modules.q_b_proj
        self.q_proj = mla_modules.q_proj
        self.kv_a_layernorm = mla_modules.kv_a_layernorm
        self.kv_b_proj = mla_modules.kv_b_proj
        self.rotary_emb = mla_modules.rotary_emb
        self.o_proj = mla_modules.o_proj
        self.indexer = mla_modules.indexer
        self.indexer_rope_emb = mla_modules.indexer_rotary_emb
        self.is_sparse = mla_modules.is_sparse

        # Whether to skip top-k token selection computation in this layer.
        # When True, the indexer will not be called, and the layer will reuse
        # the topk_tokens buffer written by a previous layer in the same pass.
        # Refer: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.12201 for more details.
        self.skip_topk = skip_topk
        # qrep is active when the query projection is a DCP-group-sharded layer
        # that materializes the full group head set locally.
        q_proj_layer = self.q_b_proj if self.q_lora_rank is not None else self.q_proj
        self.dcp_q_replicate = getattr(q_proj_layer, "qrep_active", False)
        if self.indexer is not None:
            assert hasattr(self.indexer, "topk_tokens")
            self.topk_tokens = self.indexer.topk_tokens
            self.topk_indices_buffer = mla_modules.topk_indices_buffer

        self.mla_attn = MLAAttention(
            num_heads=self.num_heads,
            scale=scale,
            qk_nope_head_dim=self.qk_nope_head_dim,
            qk_rope_head_dim=self.qk_rope_head_dim,
            v_head_dim=self.v_head_dim,
            q_lora_rank=self.q_lora_rank,
            kv_lora_rank=self.kv_lora_rank,
            cache_config=cache_config,
            quant_config=quant_config,
            prefix=f"{prefix}.attn",
            kv_b_proj=self.kv_b_proj,
            dcp_q_replicate=self.dcp_q_replicate,
            use_sparse=self.is_sparse,
            indexer=self.indexer,
            topk_indices_buffer=mla_modules.topk_indices_buffer,
        )

        self.prefix = prefix

    def forward(
        self,
        positions: torch.Tensor,
        hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
        llama_4_scaling: torch.Tensor | None = None,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        q_c = None
        kv_lora = None

        if self.q_lora_rank is not None:
            assert self.fused_qkv_a_proj is not None, (
                "fused_qkv_a_proj is required when q_lora_rank is not None"
            )
            assert self.q_a_layernorm is not None, (
                "q_a_layernorm is required when q_lora_rank is not None"
            )
            assert self.q_b_proj is not None, (
                "q_b_proj is required when q_lora_rank is not None"
            )

            qkv_lora = self.fused_qkv_a_proj(hidden_states)[0]
            q_c, kv_lora = qkv_lora.split(
                [self.q_lora_rank, self.kv_lora_rank + self.qk_rope_head_dim],
                dim=-1,
            )
            q_c = self.q_a_layernorm(q_c)
            q_proj_layer = self.q_b_proj
            q_proj_input = q_c
        else:
            assert self.kv_a_proj_with_mqa is not None, (
                "kv_a_proj_with_mqa is required when q_lora_rank is None"
            )
            assert self.q_proj is not None, (
                "q_proj is required when q_lora_rank is None"
            )
            kv_lora = self.kv_a_proj_with_mqa(hidden_states)[0]
            q_proj_layer = self.q_proj
            q_proj_input = hidden_states

        kv_c, k_pe = kv_lora.split([self.kv_lora_rank, self.qk_rope_head_dim], dim=-1)
        kv_c_normed = self.kv_a_layernorm(kv_c)
        # Add head dim of 1 to k_pe
        k_pe = k_pe.unsqueeze(1)

        q = q_proj_layer(q_proj_input)[0]
        heads = self.num_heads
        if self.dcp_q_replicate:
            heads *= q_proj_layer.group_size
        q = q.view(-1, heads, self.qk_head_dim)

        if self.rotary_emb is not None:
            q[..., self.qk_nope_head_dim :], k_pe = self.rotary_emb(
                positions, q[..., self.qk_nope_head_dim :], k_pe
            )

        if self.indexer and self.is_sparse and not self.skip_topk:
            self.indexer(hidden_states, q_c, positions, self.indexer_rope_emb)

        if llama_4_scaling is not None:
            q *= llama_4_scaling

        q_dcp_replicated = None
        if self.dcp_q_replicate:
            q_dcp_replicated, q = q, q_proj_layer._local_view(q)

        attn_out = self.mla_attn(
            q,
            kv_c_normed,
            k_pe,
            output_shape=(hidden_states.shape[0], self.num_heads * self.v_head_dim),
            q_dcp_replicated=q_dcp_replicated,
        )

        return self.o_proj(attn_out)[0]
"}}]

TEST PLAN V1 REVIEW — Generalized fused_a_gemm Port (Proposal #1)
================================================================================
Model: nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 | GPU: NVIDIA B200 | TP=4 | BS=1, ISL=4, OSL=1024
Port Plan: /sandbox/vllm/codegen-out/code_port_plan/V1_review.txt
================================================================================

OVERVIEW

This test plan covers the port of SGLang's generalized fused_a_gemm kernel to
vLLM, including JIT compilation, relaxed alignment-based shape gating, Q-B
projection support, and the VLLM_DISABLE_FUSED_A_GEMM_GENERAL kill-switch.

Test files are organized by tier:
  Tier 1: Unit tests (kernel correctness, no model loading)
  Tier 2: Integration tests (custom op dispatch, gating logic, kill-switch)
  Tier 3: End-to-end tests (model inference, accuracy, performance)


================================================================================
SECTION 1: UNIT TESTS — JIT KERNEL COMPILATION AND CORRECTNESS
================================================================================

File: tests/kernels/test_dsv3_fused_a_gemm_jit.py
Requires: SM90+ GPU, CUDA toolkit for JIT compilation
Skip condition: not current_platform.is_cuda() or
                not current_platform.has_device_capability(90)

Test framework pattern follows existing tests/kernels/ conventions:
  - pytest parametrize for shapes, batch sizes, dtypes
  - torch.testing.assert_close for numerical comparison
  - Reference implementation: torch.nn.functional.linear (cuBLAS)

1.1 test_jit_kernel_compilation
    Purpose: Verify JIT compilation succeeds for all supported shapes.
    Shapes to compile:
      (hd_in=7168, hd_out=2112)   # DeepSeek-V3 (existing AOT shape, verify JIT also works)
      (hd_in=6144, hd_out=2624)   # GLM-5.2 QKV-A (q_lora_rank=2048)
      (hd_in=2048, hd_out=6144)   # GLM-5.2 Q-B (q_lora_rank=2048)
    Assertion: _load_jit_module(hd_in, hd_out) returns a module with
              dsv3_fused_a_gemm_jit callable.
    Notes:
      - First call triggers compilation (10-30s); subsequent calls use cache.
      - Test must verify lru_cache deduplication: calling twice returns same object.

1.2 test_jit_kernel_correctness_qkv_a_shapes
    Purpose: Verify kernel produces correct output for QKV-A projection shapes.
    Parameters:
      shapes: [(6144, 2624)]
      num_tokens: [1, 2, 4, 8, 9, 16]  # boundary: 8 (tile_n switch), 16 (max)
    Implementation:
      input_ = torch.randn(num_tokens, hd_in, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
      weight = torch.randn(hd_out, hd_in, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
      ref = torch.nn.functional.linear(input_, weight)
      # Call JIT kernel: expects (mat_a=[M, hd_in], mat_b=[hd_in, hd_out] = weight.T)
      from vllm.model_executor.kernels.linear.dsv3_fused_a_gemm_jit import (
          dsv3_fused_a_gemm_jit,
      )
      out = dsv3_fused_a_gemm_jit(input_, weight.T)
      torch.testing.assert_close(out, ref, rtol=1e-2, atol=1e-2)
    Why rtol=1e-2:
      BF16 inputs with FP32 accumulation can differ from cuBLAS due to different
      summation order. 1e-2 is the tolerance used by existing vLLM kernel tests
      (see test_fused_deepseek_v32_norm_rope.py).

1.3 test_jit_kernel_correctness_q_b_shapes
    Purpose: Verify kernel produces correct output for Q-B projection shapes.
    Parameters:
      shapes: [(2048, 6144)]
      num_tokens: [1, 2, 4, 8, 9, 16]
    Implementation: Same pattern as 1.2 but with Q-B shapes.
    Note: These shapes have larger hd_out (6144), testing tile_m=32 path
          (per pick_tile_m function).

1.4 test_jit_kernel_correctness_dsv3_shape
    Purpose: Verify JIT kernel is bit-compatible with existing AOT kernel for DSV3.
    Parameters:
      shape: (7168, 2112)
      num_tokens: [1, 4, 8, 16]
    Implementation:
      input_ = torch.randn(num_tokens, 7168, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
      weight = torch.randn(2112, 7168, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
      # AOT kernel
      output_aot = torch.empty(num_tokens, 2112, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
      ops.dsv3_fused_a_gemm(output_aot, input_, weight.T)
      # JIT kernel

5.1 test_cuda_graph_capture_and_replay
    Purpose: Verify JIT kernel can be captured and replayed in a CUDA graph.
    Implementation:
      # Warmup (triggers JIT compilation outside graph)
      input_ = torch.randn(1, 6144, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
      weight_t = torch.randn(6144, 2624, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
      warmup_out = dsv3_fused_a_gemm_jit(input_, weight_t)

      # Capture
      g = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
      with torch.cuda.graph(g):
          graph_out = dsv3_fused_a_gemm_jit(input_, weight_t)

      # Replay with new data
      input_.copy_(torch.randn_like(input_))
      g.replay()

      # Compute reference with the new input data
      ref = input_ @ weight_t  # [1, 6144] @ [6144, 2624] = [1, 2624]
      torch.testing.assert_close(graph_out, ref, rtol=1e-2, atol=1e-2)

    Notes:
      - JIT compilation MUST NOT occur inside CUDA graph capture.
      - The warmup call ensures the module is compiled and cached.
      - This test validates that the kernel's launch pattern (cudaLaunchKernelEx
        with PDL) is CUDA-graph-compatible.

5.2 test_cuda_graph_with_varying_batch_size
    Purpose: Verify CUDA graph works with max batch size and smaller replays.
    Implementation:
      Capture graph with num_tokens=16 (padded max).
      Replay with effective batch sizes 1, 4, 8, 16 by zero-padding input.
      Compare output[:effective_bs] against reference.
    Note: CUDA graphs require fixed tensor sizes, so the capture uses the max
      batch size and the actual batch size is handled by the kernel internally
      (only num_tokens rows are computed).

[{"time_unix_nano":1786490816475545247,"name":"tool.output","attributes":{"file_path":"/sandbox/vllm/codegen-out/test_plan/V1_review_summary.txt","content":"================================================================================
TEST PLAN V1 REVIEW SUMMARY
================================================================================

8 issues found. All corrected in V1_review.txt.

ISSUE 1 (Shape error): Skip condition uses capability(89), should be capability(90)
  Location: Section 1 skip condition, Section 11.1 pytest marker
  Problem: The codebase uses is_device_capability(90) for SM90+ (Hopper).
    Capability 89 is Ada Lovelace (SM89), which does NOT support the wgmma
    instructions this kernel requires. Using 89 would let the test run on
    hardware that cannot execute the kernel, causing CUDA errors.
  Fix: Changed has_device_capability(89) to has_device_capability(90) in both
    the skip condition and the pytest marker.

ISSUE 2 (Phantom shape): Tests include (6144, 2112) shape that does not exist
  Location: Sections 1.1, 1.2, 1.7, 3.2, 3.8, 8.1
  Problem: The test plan includes shape (hd_in=6144, hd_out=2112) labeled as
    "GLM-5.2 QKV-A (q_lora_rank=1536)". However, the user-provided correct
    shapes state QKV-A weight is [2624, 6144] (q_lora_rank=2048). The shape
    (2112, 6144) is unverified and including it bloats compilation time with
    a shape that may never be used. The port plan allowlist includes it
    defensively, but the test plan should focus on verified shapes.
  Fix: Removed (6144, 2112) from test 1.1 compilation list, removed from 1.2
    parametrize, removed from 1.7 caching test, removed from 3.2 and 3.8 shape
    lists. Kept only the verified shapes: (6144, 2624) for QKV-A and
    (2048, 6144) for Q-B.

ISSUE 3 (Phantom shape): Tests include (1536, 6144) Q-B shape
  Location: Sections 1.1, 1.3, 3.6, 8.2
  Problem: Same rationale as Issue 2. The user states q_lora_rank=2048, giving
    Q-B shape [6144, 2048]. The (1536, 6144) variant is unverified.
  Fix: Removed (1536, 6144) from compilation list, correctness tests, gate
    tests, and benchmarks. Only (2048, 6144) remains.

ISSUE 4 (Benchmark shape error): benchmark_kernel_latency_qkv_a lists (6144, 2112)
  Location: Section 8.1
  Problem: Includes phantom shape (6144, 2112). Same as Issue 2.
  Fix: Removed. Only (6144, 2624) and (7168, 2112) remain.

ISSUE 5 (Count mismatch): "5 supported shapes" referenced but only 3 verified
  Location: Section 8.3
  Problem: References "All 5 supported shapes" but with phantom shapes removed,
    there are only 3: (7168, 2112), (6144, 2624), (2048, 6144).
  Fix: Changed to "All 3 supported shapes".

ISSUE 6 (Allowlist assertion): test_allowlist_completeness asserts wrong set
  Location: Section 3.8
  Problem: Asserts _SUPPORTED_FUSED_A_GEMM_SHAPES contains (2112, 6144) which
    is a phantom shape. Should only contain verified shapes.
  Fix: Changed expected set to {(2112, 7168), (2624, 6144)}.

ISSUE 7 (Missing test): No test for non-contiguous mat_b (weight.T)
  Location: Section 9.4
  Problem: Test 9.4 tests non-contiguous mat_a but not non-contiguous mat_b.
    In practice, weight.T produces a non-contiguous tensor (it is a transposed
    view). The kernel receives mat_b = weight.T which is column-major (non-
    contiguous in row-major PyTorch convention). This is the NORMAL usage path
    and is already tested implicitly in every other test that calls
    dsv3_fused_a_gemm_jit(input_, weight.T). No additional test needed since
    all existing tests already cover this path. Noted but no change required.

ISSUE 8 (CUDA graph test): Reference computation comment is confusing
  Location: Section 5.1
  Problem: The original had confusing comments about F.linear vs matmul for
    the reference computation after graph replay. The code first writes
    "ref = F.linear(input_, weight_t.T)" with a note, then overwrites with
    "ref = input_ @ weight_t". This is correct (input_ @ weight_t matches
    what the kernel computes) but the dead code and comments are confusing.
  Fix: Removed the dead F.linear line and clarified the comment.

) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Dynamically run min-latency gemm if num_tokens <= 16.
    This must be wrapped in a custom op because our torch.compile integration
    does not support runtime dispatching on num_tokens.
    """
    num_tokens = input_.shape[0]
    if 0 < num_tokens <= 16:
        output = torch.empty(
            num_tokens,
            weight.shape[0],
            dtype=torch.bfloat16,
            device=input_.device,
        )
        ops.dsv3_fused_a_gemm(output, input_, weight.T)
        return output
    else:
        return torch.nn.functional.linear(input_, weight)


def _min_latency_fused_qkv_a_proj_fake(
    input_: torch.Tensor,
    weight: torch.Tensor,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    return input_.new_empty(input_.shape[0], weight.shape[0])


direct_register_custom_op(
    op_name="min_latency_fused_qkv_a_proj",
    op_func=_min_latency_fused_qkv_a_proj_impl,

    fake_impl=_min_latency_fused_qkv_a_proj_fake,
)


class DeepSeekV2FusedQkvAProjLinear(MergedColumnParallelLinear):
    def __init__(
        self,
        input_size: int,
        output_size: list[int],
        quant_config: QuantizationConfig | None = None,
        prefix: str = "",
    ):
        super().__init__(
            input_size,
            output_size,
            bias=False,
            quant_config=quant_config,
            disable_tp=True,
            prefix=prefix,
        )

        # Check if the DeepSeek V3 fused A GEMM kernel can be used.
        # This kernel supports PDL and is optimized for low batch size.
        self._use_min_latency_gemm = (
            hasattr(self, "weight")
            and self.weight.dtype == torch.bfloat16
            and self.weight.shape[0] == 2112
            and self.weight.shape[1] == 7168
            and current_platform.is_cuda()
            and (
                current_platform.is_device_capability(90)
                or current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100)
            )
        )

    def forward(

## Goal
# Goal: generalize vLLM's `fused_a_gemm` for the GLM-5.2 QKV-A + Q-B projections

Port SGLang's shape-general fused A-GEMM into vLLM so the GLM-5.2 QKV-A and Q-B projections stop
falling back to the generic linear path. This is proposal **#1** of the cross-trace improvement plan
(P0, est. **-7520 ns/layer**, -7.0% of block time, difficulty MEDIUM-HIGH).

The brief is authoritative and measurement-derived: it comes from a paired vLLM/SGLang nsys capture of
the SAME model, hardware and workload, where vLLM is 21.2 us/layer (19.7%) slower than SGLang on the
dominant SharedIndexer block. Read `brief.md` for the full proposal text, including the exact
before/after code and the two hard-coded gates.

## Frozen experiment identity

| | |
|---|---|
| Model | `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` |
| Hardware | 4x NVIDIA B200, TP=4 |
| Workload | BS=1, ISL=4, OSL=1024 (pure decode, low latency) |
| Target | vLLM v0.25.1 (V1 engine), commit `b07ec92faa2d534ed97fe97f44ca71c816404849` |
| Reference | SGLang, commit `d6ef68881e263812d4901f632786015005c4d050` |

NVFP4 is Blackwell-only: this brief cannot be graded on Hopper, and a candidate that only compiles is
not a candidate. The gate measures on the same 4x B200 shape the brief was captured on.

Drive the vendored `ai_auto_analyze` code-gen pipeline; do not hand-port the kernel yourself. The
pipeline holds the domain expertise (the port-plan / test-plan / code-gen / runtime-iteration phases
and their review criteria) and its runtime phases are configured for `runtime_backend: "delegated"`,
so every GPU action goes through the broker's codegen tools rather than a local GPU you do not have.

The cross-trace analysis is vendored at `cross-trace/` in your workspace: pass
`cross-trace/cross_trace_config.json` as the config. The pipeline is on the default import path via a
`.pth`, so `common.skill_helpers` and `auto_code_gen.run_code_gen` import with no PYTHONPATH.

The interpreter is `python3`; this sandbox has no `python` and no venv. Where the vendored skills
write `python -m ...`, run `python3 -m ...`. A `python: not found` is that gap, not a missing
pipeline.

**Run the command; do not look for the file first.** You are landlock-confined to your workspace,
and the pipeline lives at `/opt/ai_auto_analyze`, outside it. A `find` proves nothing about what you
can import — the only test that means anything is running `python3 -m common.skill_helpers ...` and
reading its error. If the import genuinely fails, report it and stop. Do not hand-author the
code-gen config and do not hand-port the kernel.

1. `/prepare-code-gen cross-trace/cross_trace_config.json 1` to generate the code-gen config.

4. **A/B attribution** — the same digest re-measured with the kill-switch set. Advisory, but it is

5. **Mechanism (advisory)** — an nsys capture over the frozen workload. The brief predicts a specific

[{"time_unix_nano":1786493427101548144,"name":"tool.output","attributes":{"file_path":"/sandbox/vllm/vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v2.py","content":"class DeepSeekV2FusedQkvAProjLinear(MergedColumnParallelLinear):
    def __init__(
        self,
        input_size: int,
        output_size: list[int],
        quant_config: QuantizationConfig | None = None,
        prefix: str = "",
    ):
        super().__init__(
            input_size,
            output_size,
            bias=False,
            quant_config=quant_config,
            disable_tp=True,
            prefix=prefix,
        )

        # Check if the DeepSeek V3 fused A GEMM kernel can be used.
        # This kernel supports PDL and is optimized for low batch size.
        self._use_min_latency_gemm = (
            hasattr(self, "weight")
            and self.weight.dtype == torch.bfloat16
            and self.weight.shape[0] == 2112
            and self.weight.shape[1] == 7168
            and current_platform.is_cuda()
            and (
                current_platform.is_device_capability(90)
                or current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100)
            )
        )

    def forward(
        self,
        input_,
    ) -> torch.Tensor | tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.nn.Parameter | None]:
        if self._use_min_latency_gemm:
            output = torch.ops.vllm.min_latency_fused_qkv_a_proj(input_, self.weight)
            if not self.return_bias:
                return output
            output_bias = self.bias if self.skip_bias_add else None
            return output, output_bias
        else:
            # Fallback to the standard forward method when
            # the fused A GEMM kernel cannot be used.
            return super().forward(input_)

    """Linear method without quantization."""

    def create_weights(
        self,
        layer: torch.nn.Module,
        input_size_per_partition: int,
        output_partition_sizes: list[int],
        input_size: int,
        output_size: int,
        params_dtype: torch.dtype,
        **extra_weight_attrs,
    ):
        # This method creates unquantized linear weights.
        # The weights are not quantized, and they are not sharded.
        # The amount of memory allocated for the weights is
        # sum(output_partition_sizes) * input_size_per_partition.
        weight_loader = extra_weight_attrs.pop("weight_loader")
        weight = ModelWeightParameter(
            data=torch.empty(
                sum(output_partition_sizes),
                input_size_per_partition,
                dtype=params_dtype,
            ),
            input_dim=1,
            output_dim=0,
            weight_loader=weight_loader,
        )

        layer.register_parameter("weight", weight)
        set_weight_attrs(weight, extra_weight_attrs)

    def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer: torch.nn.Module) -> None:
        if current_platform.is_cpu():
            from vllm.model_executor.layers.utils import dispatch_cpu_unquantized_gemm

            dispatch_cpu_unquantized_gemm(layer, remove_weight=True)

    def apply(
        self,
        layer: torch.nn.Module,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        bias: torch.Tensor | None = None,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        if envs.VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT and current_platform.is_cuda_alike():
            return linear_batch_invariant(x, layer.weight, bias)
        return dispatch_unquantized_gemm()(layer, x, layer.weight, bias)

    input_: torch.Tensor,
    weight: torch.Tensor,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Dynamically run min-latency gemm if num_tokens <= 16.
    This must be wrapped in a custom op because our torch.compile integration
    does not support runtime dispatching on num_tokens.
    """
    num_tokens = input_.shape[0]
    if 0 < num_tokens <= 16:
        output = torch.empty(
            num_tokens,
            weight.shape[0],
            dtype=torch.bfloat16,
            device=input_.device,
        )
        ops.dsv3_fused_a_gemm(output, input_, weight.T)
        return output
    else:
        return torch.nn.functional.linear(input_, weight)

## Goal
# Goal: generalize vLLM's `fused_a_gemm` for the GLM-5.2 QKV-A + Q-B projections

Port SGLang's shape-general fused A-GEMM into vLLM so the GLM-5.2 QKV-A and Q-B projections stop
falling back to the generic linear path. This is proposal **#1** of the cross-trace improvement plan
(P0, est. **-7520 ns/layer**, -7.0% of block time, difficulty MEDIUM-HIGH).

The brief is authoritative and measurement-derived: it comes from a paired vLLM/SGLang nsys capture of
the SAME model, hardware and workload, where vLLM is 21.2 us/layer (19.7%) slower than SGLang on the
dominant SharedIndexer block. Read `brief.md` for the full proposal text, including the exact
before/after code and the two hard-coded gates.

## Frozen experiment identity

| | |
|---|---|
| Model | `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` |
| Hardware | 4x NVIDIA B200, TP=4 |

| Target | vLLM v0.25.1 (V1 engine), commit `b07ec92faa2d534ed97fe97f44ca71c816404849` |
| Reference | SGLang, commit `d6ef68881e263812d4901f632786015005c4d050` |

NVFP4 is Blackwell-only: this brief cannot be graded on Hopper, and a candidate that only compiles is
not a candidate. The gate measures on the same 4x B200 shape the brief was captured on.

# Goal: generalize vLLM's `fused_a_gemm` for the GLM-5.2 QKV-A + Q-B projections

falling back to the generic linear path. This is proposal **#1** of the cross-trace improvement plan
(P0, est. **-7520 ns/layer**, -7.0% of block time, difficulty MEDIUM-HIGH).

The brief is authoritative and measurement-derived: it comes from a paired vLLM/SGLang nsys capture of
the SAME model, hardware and workload, where vLLM is 21.2 us/layer (19.7%) slower than SGLang on the
dominant SharedIndexer block. Read `brief.md` for the full proposal text, including the exact
before/after code and the two hard-coded gates.

PROPOSAL #3: FIX MOE GATE ROUTER TO USE SPECIALIZED KERNEL
========================================================================================================================

Impact: -6048ns/layer (-5.6% of block time) | Priority: P0 | Difficulty: MEDIUM

  Both frameworks: gate shape (6144, 256), E=256 experts, BF16 input, FP32 output.

  torch.compile (mode 3) custom op compatibility.

      def weight_loader(self, param: Parameter, loaded_weight: torch.Tensor):

          if (loaded_weight.dtype == torch.float32
                  and self.allow_specialized_router_gemm):
              loaded_weight = loaded_weight.to(torch.bfloat16)
          super().weight_loader(param, loaded_weight)
